title: Adopted trivial-potential classical charged scalar model

items.title: Adopted trivial-potential classical charged scalar model
items.physical_scope: A smooth classical complex scalar with a globally defined real electromagnetic potential A and exact field strength F=dA, arbitrary real coupling lambda, positive scalar normalization K_phi, and smooth real self-potential V. This is the trivial-potential sector only; it is not a quantum, empirical, material-response, or coupled-solution claim.

references.title: David Tong, Gauge Theory, complete author-hosted lecture notes (457-page PDF)
references.locator: §2.5.2, PDF pp. 89–91 (printed pp. 78–80): the four-dimensional Abelian-Higgs action and its charged complex scalar covariant derivative. Only the classical functional form is used; its natural units, Higgs potential, superconducting interpretation, and quantum material claims are not imported.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), complete 97-page preprint
references.locator: §3.1, PDF pp. 22–31, and §5.4, PDF pp. 81–87: the symmetric-hyperbolic local Cauchy framework and Einstein–matter coupling, including brief charged-scalar context. The source gives no complete proof for this exact coupled system.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, eqs. (4.68)–(4.70), PDF pp. 123–124 (printed pp. 117–118), matter action and Hilbert-stress conventions; Ch. 5, eqs. (5.33)–(5.38), PDF p. 145 (printed p. 139), on-shell diffeomorphism identity. Its units and signs are not adopted.

items.title: Local evolution of the adopted classical charged scalar model
items.physical_scope: Conditional local existence and smooth local uniqueness, up to spacetime isometry and electromagnetic gauge, for the adopted Einstein–Maxwell–classical charged-scalar action in the global real-potential sector and for the stated compatible initial data. The deduction uses the current draft mathematical development result with its exact Countable Choice and Dependent Choice assumptions. It asserts no empirical validity, quantum interpretation, nontrivial bundle sector, singular-source evolution, global existence, or geodesic completeness.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Lecture Notes in Physics 540 (2000), complete 97-page preprint
references.locator: §3.1, PDF pp. 22–31, for the symmetric-hyperbolic local Cauchy framework; §5.4, PDF pp. 81–87, for Einstein–matter coupling and charged-scalar context. The source explicitly gives an outline rather than the exact coupled proof used here.

references.locator: Ch. 4, eqs. (4.68)–(4.70), PDF pp. 123–124 (printed pp. 117–118), matter action and Hilbert-stress conventions; Ch. 5, eqs. (5.33)–(5.38), PDF p. 145 (printed p. 139), on-shell diffeomorphism identity. The source conventions are not substituted for the local SI ones.
